[PAPER_0001, relevance_score=0.205] This article has been preprinted on PsyArXiv and is available at https://doi.org/mvnk. The authors have no known conflicts of interest to disclose. All experiments were preregistered. All cleaned data, analysis code, preregistrations, and research materials are available at https://osf.io/9gc3x/ (Constant & Kerzel, 2024).

Martin Constant served as lead for conceptualization, data curation, formal analysis, investigation, methodology, software, visualization, and writing-original draft.

[PAPER_0007, relevance_score=0.210] Consistent with bottom-up effects on attentional prioritization and encoding into VWM, salience was found to be a major determinant of VWM performance (Constant & Liesefeld, 2021).

Top-down processes, on the other hand, involve the goal-driven modulation of priority. Observers can willfully prioritize certain objects, features, or locations according to their current objectives while ignoring salience. For instance, the less salient stimuli in Constant and Liesefeld (2023) were probed more often and therefore had a higher top-down priority.

[PAPER_0017, relevance_score=0.268] Transparency and Openness
